fact_check.fact: Buntanetap did not meet either co-primary endpoint (ADAS-Cog11, ADCS-CGIC) vs. placebo in the 351-patient ITT population.
fact_check.note: Matches paper Table 1 and 'Primary analysis results' text directly.

fact_check.fact: ADAS-Cog11 LS mean difference 0.13 (95% CI −1.088, 1.350), p=0.833.
Key secondary ADCS-ADL difference −1.48 (95% CI −3.326, 0.375), p=0.118.
TEAEs 33.3% (86/262) buntanetap vs. 26.1% (23/88) placebo; drug-related TEAEs 8.9% (23/258) vs. 3.4% (3/88); no serious drug-related TEAEs.
~38-40% of enrolled participants lacked amyloid pathology by plasma pTau217/t-Tau testing; only 62.1% (n=216) confirmed AD pathology.
fact_check.note: 62.1%/n=216 figure is exact. Note: the paper itself is internally inconsistent, using both '~38%' (post-hoc analysis section) and '~40%' (abstract, discussion) for the same figure — this is the source's inconsistency, not an error introduced downstream.

fact_check.fact: In the post-hoc biomarker-positive mild AD subgroup (n=95), buntanetap showed a dose-dependent, nominally significant ADAS-Cog11 improvement.
fact_check.note: Matches text, but important nuance: the paper states this is improvement 'compared to baseline,' not vs. placebo — the subgroup section does not report a placebo-controlled treatment effect for ADAS-Cog11. Reflected in the takeaway wording.

fact_check.fact: Moderate AD biomarker-positive patients (n=115) showed no ADAS-Cog11 treatment-related change; no subgroup showed ADCS-CGIC benefit.
fact_check.note: Matches Fig. 2a, c, d description text.

fact_check.fact: Corresponding author and multiple co-authors are Annovis Bio employees (drug sponsor); paper states 'the authors declare no competing interests.'
fact_check.note: Correspondence email fang@annovisbio.com and 'Competing interests' statement both appear verbatim in the source.

fact_check.fact: Forest plot (Fig. 3) shows a 'consistent favorable effect' across demographic/APOE4 subgroups.
fact_check.note: Described only qualitatively in text; no point estimates or CIs given, and the figure image isn't available to check. Excluded from key findings, kept as a caveat only.

fact_check.fact: Plasma biomarkers (t-Tau, TDP43, IL5, IL6, S100A12, IFN-γ, IGF1R, NFL) trended favorably with 30mg vs. placebo; GFAP showed no effect.
fact_check.note: Reported descriptively with no p-values or formal statistical testing in the source. Kept out of key findings, noted as exploratory in caveats.

fact_check.fact: NCT06709014 (confirmatory Phase 3) is a 760-patient, biomarker-selected, 18-month study with 6-month and 18-month co-primary readouts.
fact_check.note: 760-patient/18-month figure matches paper Discussion text ('760-patient 18-month pivotal study'). Enrollment count is now disputed — see next entry.

fact_check.fact: NCT06709014 enrollment: registry lists 760 (estimated); July 2026 Annovis press release claims ~850 enrolled, reaching full enrollment.
fact_check.note: Registry has not been updated to reflect the sponsor's later enrollment claim. Flagged in trial_evidence_md and the NCT06709014 trial page rather than silently picking one number.

fact_check.fact: NCT06709014 primary endpoints are ADAS-Cog13 and ADCS-iADL.
fact_check.note: Not stated in the source paper text (which only gives readout timing); sourced from the trials researcher's registry check, marked 'verified: registry' on their end but not independently re-checked by me against ClinicalTrials.gov directly.

research_page.title: Buntanetap in mild-to-moderate AD (phase 2/3)
research_page.description: Oral APP/Tau translation inhibitor missed its co-primary cognitive endpoints in the full trial population; a small post-hoc biomarker-positive subgroup showed a signal.
research_page.authors_line_md: Fang et al. — sponsor: Annovis Bio; corresponding author and several co-authors are Annovis Bio employees
research_page.takeaway_md: Buntanetap (an oral APP/Tau translation inhibitor) missed both co-primary cognitive endpoints against placebo in the full 351-patient trial. A post-hoc plasma-biomarker check found ~40% of enrollees lacked amyloid pathology; restricted to the 95 biomarker-confirmed mild-AD patients, buntanetap showed a dose-dependent improvement in ADAS-Cog11 versus baseline — not versus placebo, and from an unregistered, non-multiplicity-corrected subgroup carved out of a dataset that had already failed its primary hypothesis. Safety was favorable, with no serious drug-related adverse events. A confirmatory, biomarker-selected Phase 3 ([NCT06709014](/trials/buntanetap-nct06709014)) is underway, with readout not expected before 2027–2028.
key_findings_md: Both co-primary endpoints missed in the ITT population: ADAS-Cog11 LS mean difference 0.13 (95% CI −1.09, 1.35), p=0.833; ADCS-CGIC difference 0.22 (95% CI −0.07, 0.52), p=0.141 (paper, Table 1)

In the post-hoc biomarker-positive mild AD subgroup (n=95), buntanetap showed a dose-dependent, nominally significant ADAS-Cog11 improvement versus baseline — not a placebo-controlled result, and not prespecified (paper, Fig. 2b)
Moderate AD biomarker-positive patients (n=115) showed no treatment-related change on ADAS-Cog11; no biomarker-positive subgroup showed benefit on ADCS-CGIC (paper, Fig. 2a, c, d)
Plasma pTau217/t-Tau testing found only 62.1% (n=216) of enrollees had confirmed AD pathology despite meeting clinical inclusion criteria (paper, Post-hoc analysis section)
Treatment-emergent adverse events: 33.3% buntanetap (all doses) vs. 26.1% placebo; drug-related TEAEs 8.9% vs. 3.4%; no serious drug-related adverse events (paper, Safety section)
research_page.methods_md: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, dose-ranging Phase 2/3 trial ([NCT05686044](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05686044)); 351 patients with mild-to-moderate AD (MMSE 14-24, ages 55-85) at 54 US sites, randomized 1:1:1:1 to 7.5mg, 15mg, 30mg buntanetap or placebo for 12 weeks. No biomarker or imaging confirmation of amyloid pathology was required for enrollment.
research_page.trial_evidence_md: NCT05686044 is buntanetap's only completed AD efficacy trial, and it failed its prespecified primary hypothesis. The sponsor's confirmatory Phase 3, [NCT06709014](/trials/buntanetap-nct06709014), enrolls only biomarker-confirmed early-AD patients — directly testing the post-hoc subgroup hypothesis from this paper — with primary completion not expected before 2027-2028. Every buntanetap AD and Parkinson's trial to date is sponsored solely by Annovis Bio, and none has an independently replicated peer-reviewed primary efficacy result. A July 2026 Annovis press release claims NCT06709014 reached full enrollment at roughly 850 patients, above the registry's still-listed estimate of 760 — the registry record hasn't caught up.
research_page.sentiment_md: Public discussion concentrates in investor and trade-press circles; searches found no meaningful discussion in patient or caregiver forums. Patient-facing trade outlets like [Alzheimer's News Today](https://alzheimersnewstoday.com/news/buntanetap-found-effective-safe-early-alzheimers-trial-data/) framed the results as a straightforward efficacy win, while financial press ([FierceBiotech](https://www.fiercebiotech.com/biotech/annovis-shares-plummet-more-40-after-muddled-alzheimers-readout)) has repeatedly flagged Annovis's pattern of emphasizing post-hoc subgroups when primary endpoints fail, across this and two prior buntanetap readouts.
caveats_md: The headline subgroup finding (n=95) is post-hoc and unregistered, drawn from the same dataset that failed the prespecified primary hypothesis in the full ITT population — a data-dependent selection that 'nominal significance' does not resolve
The reported subgroup benefit is versus baseline, not versus placebo; a treatment-vs-placebo effect was not demonstrated in this subgroup
Not adjusted for multiplicity across a subgroup analysis or an 8+ analyte exploratory biomarker panel; GFAP showed no treatment effect and is not emphasized in the discussion
Corresponding author and several co-authors are Annovis Bio employees (the trial sponsor), yet the paper states 'the authors declare no competing interests'
Forest-plot (subgroup-consistency) and biomarker-trend claims are described only qualitatively, with no p-values, effect sizes, or figure data available for independent verification
Raw trial data are withheld until an NDA filing, limiting independent reanalysis
relates_to_md: [Biomarkers](/research/biomarkers) — plasma pTau217 testing drove the post-hoc reclassification of roughly 40% of enrollees as amyloid-negative
[Amyloid hypothesis](/research/amyloid-hypothesis) — buntanetap targets APP synthesis upstream of amyloid plaque formation, a non-antibody mechanism
[Trial tracker](/trials) — track the confirmatory Phase 3 readout

trial_pages.title: Buntanetap Phase 2/3 in mild-to-moderate AD (NCT05686044)
trial_pages.description: Oral APP/Tau translation inhibitor, Phase 2/3, 351 patients with mild-to-moderate AD; missed co-primary endpoints.
trial_pages.drug: Buntanetap / Posiphen (oral inhibitor of APP, Tau, alpha-synuclein, TDP-43 mRNA translation)
trial_pages.population: Adults 55-85 with mild-to-moderate probable AD (MMSE 14-24), n=351, no biomarker confirmation required at enrollment
trial_pages.primary_endpoint: Change in ADAS-Cog11 from baseline to week 12; ADCS-CGIC score at week 12 (co-primary)
trial_pages.why_md: Tests whether an oral, non-antibody small molecule targeting APP/Tau translation can improve cognition in mild-to-moderate AD — an alternative mechanism to the monoclonal antibodies covered on the [amyloid hypothesis](/research/amyloid-hypothesis) page. Its post-hoc biomarker-positive subgroup finding directly motivated the confirmatory [NCT06709014](/trials/buntanetap-nct06709014).
status_log_md: **2023-04** — Trial begins enrollment across 54 US sites
**2026-04** — Full results published in [npj Dementia](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44400-026-00073-z); both co-primary endpoints missed in the ITT population
trial_pages.results_md: Missed both co-primary endpoints (ADAS-Cog11, ADCS-CGIC) in the 351-patient ITT population. A post-hoc subgroup of 95 biomarker-confirmed mild-AD patients showed a nominally significant, dose-dependent ADAS-Cog11 improvement versus baseline; not prespecified or multiplicity-corrected. Well tolerated, with no serious drug-related adverse events. See [Buntanetap in mild-to-moderate AD](/research/papers/buntanetap-phase-2-3-ad).

trial_pages.title: Buntanetap pivotal Phase 3 in early AD (NCT06709014)
trial_pages.description: Biomarker-selected confirmatory Phase 3 of buntanetap 30mg in early AD, testing the NCT05686044 subgroup hypothesis.
trial_pages.population: Adults 55-85 with early AD (2024 NIA-AA criteria), MMSE 20-28, biomarker-confirmed amyloid/pTau217-positive; registry estimate n=760, sponsor reports ~850 enrolled as of July 2026
trial_pages.primary_endpoint: ADAS-Cog13 and ADCS-iADL at 6-month and 18-month co-primary readouts
trial_pages.readout: Primary completion estimated 2027-12; study completion estimated 2028-06
trial_pages.why_md: Confirmatory test of the biomarker-selection hypothesis raised by the post-hoc subgroup finding in [NCT05686044](/trials/buntanetap-nct05686044) — this time with prespecified, biomarker-confirmed enrollment and adequate statistical power. Its outcome determines whether buntanetap's mild-AD signal replicates.
status_log_md: **2026-07-07** — Annovis reports full enrollment reached (~850 patients per [press release](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/07/07/3323032/0/en/Annovis-Reaches-Full-Enrollment-in-Pivotal-Phase-3-Trial-of-Buntanetap-for-Early-Alzheimer-s-Disease.html), above the registry's 760 estimate)

timeline_entries.title: 2026-04 — Buntanetap Phase 2/3 misses primary endpoint, biomarker subgroup shows signal
timeline_entries.body_md: An oral APP/Tau translation inhibitor failed its co-primary cognitive endpoints in the full trial population; a post-hoc, unvalidated biomarker-positive subgroup showed improvement, motivating a confirmatory Phase 3 — see [Buntanetap in mild-to-moderate AD](/research/papers/buntanetap-phase-2-3-ad).

notes_for_editor: The source paper itself is internally inconsistent about the amyloid-negative rate, citing both '~38%' (post-hoc analysis section) and '~40%' (abstract, discussion) for the same underlying figure (62.1%/n=216 confirmed). Used '~40%' per the abstract/discussion framing since that's the number most secondary coverage cites, but flagging the paper's own inconsistency.

Added a trial page for NCT06709014 even though its relation_to_document is 'related-program' rather than 'reported-here' — justified because it's the pivotal confirmatory trial directly testing this paper's central post-hoc hypothesis, similar in weight to AHEAD 3-45/TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 3. Worth a second opinion on whether that's the right call under the 'trial pages' standard.
No PubMed record could be found for this paper (per analyst's search); source_line_md omits a PubMed link rather than guessing one.

NCT06709014 enrollment count is disputed between the registry (760, estimated) and a July 2026 Annovis press release (~850, 'full enrollment'). Both figures are surfaced rather than silently picking one; registry should be rechecked periodically as it's the authoritative source once updated.
